## Purpose and scope

This protocol removes the leftover primers and nucleotides from PCR products and prepares the cleaned products, with their sequencing primer, for Sanger sequencing by an external provider. It follows the barcode PCR and precedes the analysis of the chromatograms (EnGeL-BIOINF-SANGER) in the [single-specimen barcoding workflow](../../workflows/single-specimen-barcoding.qmd). The barcode PCR itself is a separate protocol [TO CONFIRM: to be written].

Three clean-up options are in use; ExoSAP-IT Express is the usual one.

## Principle

After PCR, the reaction still contains unused primers and dNTPs, which would take part in the sequencing reaction and spoil the read. Exonuclease I digests single-stranded DNA (the leftover primers) and shrimp alkaline phosphatase removes the phosphates of the dNTPs. Both enzymes are then inactivated by heat, so the product can go straight into the sequencing reaction without a column or bead clean-up. The template only works if the PCR gave a single, sharp band: other bands or smears give mixed signals in the chromatogram.

## Before you start

| Item | Details |
|:--|:--|
| Input | PCR products checked on a gel |
| Hands-on time | [TO CONFIRM] |
| Total time | About 10 min with ExoSAP-IT Express; about 30 min with ExoSAP-IT; about 1 h with the home-made mix (incubation), plus sample preparation |
| Prepare in advance | Sequencing primers diluted (Calculations); sequencing order and sample names prepared with the provider [TO CONFIRM: provider and ordering procedure]; samples entered in your sheet of the Sanger recording file |

::: {.callout-important title="CRITICAL"}
Check every PCR product on a gel first. Only products with one clear, sharp band of the expected size are sent. Products with several bands or smears give unreadable chromatograms whatever the clean-up.
:::

## Reagent preparation

- **ExoSAP-IT Express and ExoSAP-IT:** store at −20 °C (non-frost-free freezer); keep on ice while in use and return to the freezer straight away.
- **Sequencing primer:** dilute the stock so that 5 µL contain 10 pmol (2 µM; see Calculations). Prepare enough for all samples of the order.

## Procedure

### Before starting

{{< include ../../includes/_contamination-control.qmd >}}

### 1. Judge the PCR products

(@) Look at the gel image of each PCR product. Mark it as **strong** (clear, bright band) or **faint** (visible but weak band). Products without a single band of the expected size are not sent.

### 2. Clean up the PCR products

Choose one option and use it for the whole order.

**Option A: ExoSAP-IT Express (usual)**

(@) Mix 5 µL of PCR product with 2 µL of ExoSAP-IT Express on ice.
(@) In the thermocycler: 37 °C for 4 min, 80 °C for 1 min, then hold at 4 °C.

**Option B: ExoSAP-IT**

(@) Mix 5 µL of PCR product with 2 µL of ExoSAP-IT on ice.
(@) Run the ExoSAP-IT programme (about 30 min in total) [TO CONFIRM: temperatures and times from the ExoSAP-IT user guide].

**Option C: home-made Exonuclease I and SAP mix**

(@) Per sample, mix 1 µL SAP (1 U/µL), 0.25 µL Exonuclease I (20 U/µL) and 3.75 µL nuclease-free water, and add 15 µL of PCR product (20 µL in total).
(@) In the thermocycler, with the heated lid switched off: 37 °C for 40–45 min, 80 °C for 15 min, then hold at 4 °C.

> **PAUSE POINT.** Cleaned products can be kept at −20 °C (ExoSAP-IT Express user guide).

### 3. Prepare the sequencing samples

(@) For each product and each primer, label a 1.5 mL tube with the sample name agreed with the provider.
(@) Pipette the cleaned product and water:

| Band | Cleaned product | Nuclease-free water |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Strong | 1 µL | 4 µL |
| Faint | 2.5 µL | 2.5 µL |

(@) Add 5 µL of diluted primer (10 pmol). Total volume: 10 µL.
(@) If more volume is needed, scale all three volumes by 1.5 (total 15 µL) [TO CONFIRM: when the 1.5× volumes are used].
(@) Close, spin briefly and keep at 4 °C (fridge) until shipping.

### 4. Record and send

(@) Complete your sheet in the Sanger recording file (see Data and metadata) before the samples leave the lab.
(@) Send the samples to the provider [TO CONFIRM: provider (Eurofins, StabVida), tube or plate service, who places the orders and how shipments are labelled].

### After finishing

{{< include ../../includes/_before-you-leave.qmd >}}

## Calculations

**Primer dilution.** The sample receives 10 pmol of primer in 5 µL, i.e. a concentration of

$$c = \frac{n}{V} = \frac{10\ \text{pmol}}{5\ \text{µL}} = 2\ \text{pmol/µL} = 2\ \text{µM}$$

To prepare it from a stock, $V_\text{stock} = c \times V_\text{final} / c_\text{stock}$, where $c$ is the target concentration (µM), $V_\text{final}$ the volume needed (µL) and $c_\text{stock}$ the stock concentration (µM).

**Worked example.** For 20 samples (100 µL of diluted primer, with excess 110 µL) from a 10 µM stock: $V_\text{stock} = 2 \times 110 / 10 = 22$ µL of stock plus 88 µL of nuclease-free water.

## Quality control

| Control | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| PCR band on the gel | Template quality | One clear, sharp band of the expected size; strong or faint decides the volume (step 3) |
| Clean-up | Primers and dNTPs removed | Programme run to the end, including the 80 °C inactivation |
| Sequence quality | Overall result | Read quality and identification checked in EnGeL-BIOINF-SANGER |

## Data and metadata

Each person records their samples in their own sheet of the Sanger recording file, named with their full name and built from the template sheet. Only the curator (Luís Cunha) merges the personal sheets into the "All" sheet, after checking them; nobody else edits "All". The columns follow the template, which is also the sample sheet read by the Sanger pipeline (EnGeL-BIOINF-SANGER): plate or order code, well or tube code, primer pair, specimen ID and putative species and family.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- Specimen ID (EnGeL label) and DNA extract; PCR date and primer pair
- Band strength (strong or faint) and clean-up option used
- Primer sent with each sample; provider, order number, plate or tube code and position
- Date sent; operator
:::

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Noisy chromatogram from the start | Leftover primers or dNTPs | Check that the clean-up programme ran to the end; check the reagent volumes and the reagent's storage. |
| Mixed peaks along the read | Several PCR products or contamination | Send only single, sharp bands; repeat the PCR. |
| Weak or short read | Too little template | Use the faint-band volumes (2.5 µL), or repeat the PCR. |
| Sample missing in the provider's results | Sample name or position differs from the order | Check names against the order and your recording sheet. |

## Remarks

ExoSAP-IT Express is the lab's usual reagent; ExoSAP-IT and the home-made mix are also in use. Do not mix options within one order, so that results can be compared. Plate orders and tube orders give differently named files, which the Sanger pipeline handles with separate scripts (EnGeL-BIOINF-SANGER).
